🔬 BioNEST Lab, IIT Mandi Catalyst | Empowering Innovation Through Accessible Laboratory Facilities

🚀 Bridging the Gap Between Innovation and Infrastructure!

Dotasara Agrotech Private Limited, a startup incubated at the National Institute of Technology Hamirpur, recently visited the BioNEST Lab at IIT Mandi Catalyst to explore advanced laboratory facilities for product development and validation.

🌱 The startup is developing a cost-effective spectrophotometer and was looking for access to a standard spectrophotometer to validate its device by comparing readings. The team also explored access to a Voltera PCB 3D printer to support another key aspect of product development.

💡 During the visit, the team discovered the potential to access both these essential facilities under one roof, along with technical support and affordable services.

🌟 The Impact
BioNEST Lab is helping startups connect with specialised laboratory infrastructure, enabling them to overcome product development challenges, optimise costs, and accelerate innovation.

At IIT Mandi Catalyst, we are committed to making advanced laboratory facilities more accessible to startups and entrepreneurs, helping transform promising ideas into validated solutions.

From Nagpur to a National Startup Network!

Building on over two decades of experience in strengthening India’s startup ecosystem, Society for Innovation & Entrepreneurship - SINE IIT Bombay, has launched its National Hub-and-Spoke Initiative to empower incubators, connect institutions and accelerate technology-led entrepreneurship across the country.

Nagpur marks the beginning of this journey!

𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗽 𝗧𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗗𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗟𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁. 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗧𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲.

Two posts in, I have no illusions that this widespread tendering practice will change. So here is where Social Alpha stands. We raise CSR and philanthropic capital for our programs. We do not bid on RFPs or tenders. People sometimes read our reluctance as stubbornness. It is closer to self-preservation.

An RFP buys a defined service at the lowest credible price. The scope is fixed, the timeline is short, and the problem is assumed to be understood. If that assumption is wrong, no amount of efficient delivery will fix it. That market rewards execution capacity and cost. It is a good market for service providers. It is the wrong market for an innovation factory.

Our work runs the other way. The problem is uncertain. The solution is still being worked out. Science and adoption, not a budget year, set the timeline. If we bid, we would compete on price against organisations built to deliver services, and even if we won, the work would pull us away from the problems we are set up to solve. So we don’t compete for contracts. We compete for the right to solve hard problems, and for the patient, risk-tolerant capital our work demands.

When a partner’s priorities match a problem we are working on, we design together. When they do not, we part as friends, hoping that next time we will define the problem and design the program together. #SkinInTheGame

Innovation takes shape when ideas are given the right platform, guidance and opportunity to evolve into tangible solutions.

Dr.Praveen D., Head - TBI, iCreate, was part of the jury at CCSIH C2C 2.0 – Concept to Creation, organised at CHARUSAT University by the CHARUSAT Startup and Innovation Centre and CHARUSAT INNOVATIVE VENTURES FOUNDATION, in association with CCSIH.

The programme showcased 25 innovative prototypes developed by innovators, highlighting technology-driven approaches to addressing industrial challenges.

As a jury member, Dr Desai joined the evaluation of the showcased innovations, contributing his perspective to recognising promising ideas and technology-based solutions.

At iCreate, we value such collaborative platforms that nurture innovative thinking, encourage entrepreneurship and strengthen connections between academia, industry and the startup ecosystem.

What does it take to turn engineering knowledge into ideas that can make a difference?

Today, students from Rai University, Ahmedabad, visited the iCreate campus to explore the journey from innovation to entrepreneurship.

Ankush Pathania, Lead - Programmes and Events, welcomed the group. Dr.Praveen D., Head - TBI, introduced the students to iCreate’s vision, programmes and entrepreneurial ecosystem.

Dr. Raashid Saiyed, Resident Business Mentor, led an engaging session on entrepreneurial thinking, the choices that shape an idea and the mindset required to build impactful ventures. The campus tour offered students a closer look at the facilities and ecosystem that support innovation in action.

An opportunity to connect engineering knowledge with entrepreneurial thinking, explore new possibilities and look beyond the boundaries of the classroom.
